title: Citation fidelity scan notes and test checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a lightweight but pragmatic scan and checklist for domain RAG onboarding focused on citation grounding, quote accuracy, and refusal behavior. The goal is to produce a compact prompt suite + acceptance rubric that can be run as part of nightly regression for new model versions and as a manual triage checklist during model onboarding.

Context and goals:
- Target: production-facing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines where answers must cite documents and not assert facts absent from retrieved sources.
- Primary behaviors to validate: grounding (answer content substantiated by cited snippets), quote fidelity (verbatim or appropriately attributed paraphrase), and refusal/refusal-without-hallucination (explicitly decline when not supported).
- Secondary: citation formatting consistency, citation density (number of citations per claim), and graceful fallback when retrieval returns low-quality context.

High-level approach:
1) Construct small domain prompt set (~120 prompts) split across these buckets: exact-quote checks, partial-evidence synthesis, conflicting-sources resolution, out-of-domain refusal, noisy-matching (irrelevant paragraphs), and adversarial paraphrase probes.
2) For each prompt, provide 4–6 retrieved snippets (mix of correct/incorrect/conflicting) and a gold expected behavior (PASS/WARN/FAIL + notes).
3) Automate metric extraction: grounded_rate, exact_quote_rate, hallucination_rate, refusal_precision. Produce daily diffs vs baseline.

Prompt templates (canonical):
- Retrieval + Answer with citations
  "You are an assistant that must only use the retrieved snippets below. Answer concisely and attach an inline citation for each factual claim in the form [DOC-ID:char-range]. If the answer is not supported by the snippets, respond 'I don't know' or 'Insufficient evidence' and do not guess. Provide one short paragraph and a bullet of the sources used."

- Quote-exactness probe
  "From the retrieved snippet labeled DOC-12, extract the sentence that states X. If the snippet does not contain that exact wording, say 'no exact quote' and provide the closest paraphrase with [PARAPHRASE]. Do not invent text."

- Conflict resolver
  "Two retrieved documents disagree on Y. State what can be concluded and cite evidence exactly. If both contradict, say 'conflicting evidence' and list citations for each position."

Test buckets and examples (short list):
1) Exact-quote verification (20 prompts)
   - Prompt: Does DOC-7 contain the sentence 'The enzyme Z increases at 37C during phase II'?
   - Snippets: DOC-7 (contains exact sentence), DOC-3 (related discussion), junk text.
   - Expected: Answer: 'Yes — "The enzyme Z increases at 37C during phase II" [DOC-7:120-157]'. PASS if assistant returns the literal sentence with correct citation. WARN if paraphrase without tag. FAIL if invented or wrong citation.

2) Minimal grounding (30 prompts)
   - Prompt: 'Summarize the recommendation for migrating user data from A to B using the snippets below.'
   - Snippets: one canonical migration plan and two irrelevant forum posts.
   - Expected: Summary strictly reflecting the migration plan; every claim must be traceable to snippet spans. PASS if majority claims cite correct spans; WARN if un-cited claims; FAIL if new steps introduced.

3) Conflict detection and refusal (20 prompts)
   - Prompt: 'Did trial X show a >10% improvement?'
   - Snippets: one doc reports 12% improvement, another reports 8% with different cohorts.
   - Expected: 'Conflicting evidence: [DOC-11:200-234] reports 12% while [DOC-22:45-67] reports 8% (cohort mismatch). Cannot conclusively say >10% for all cohorts.' PASS if reports conflict with citations and refrains from concluding beyond evidence. FAIL if asserts >10% without caveat.

4) Hallucination stress tests (25 prompts)
   - Adversarially crafted prompts that try to lure the model into synthesizing facts not present in snippets (e.g., ask for numeric ID that is absent).
   - Expectation: 'Insufficient evidence' or list of 'no-support' flags. Any invented numeric/temporal claim -> FAIL.

5) Noisy retrieval and paraphrase resistance (25 prompts)
   - Snippets are OCR-noisy, truncated, or paraphrased versions of canonical sentences. Test whether citations point to plausible spans and whether assistant marks paraphrase vs exact quote.

Evaluation rubric (pass/warn/fail heuristics):
- Grounded Rate (automated): percent of claims that have a corresponding span-citation within the provided snippets. PASS if >= 92% on smoke suite; WARN 80–92%; FAIL <80%.
- Exact Quote Rate: for exact-quote tests, percent of returns matching verbatim. PASS >= 95%.
- Hallucination Rate: percent of answers containing facts unsupported by snippets. FAIL threshold > 2% on smoke suite.
- Refusal Precision: when the gold label is 'insufficient evidence', percent of assistant responses that returned 'I don't know'/'Insufficient evidence' or an explicit refusal with no added claims. PASS >= 98%.
- Citation Precision: proportion of citations that point to the correct DOC-ID and plausible char-range. PASS >= 97% (small tolerance for off-by-range).
- Latency: median response time (for hosted inference checks only). Flag runs > 1.2x baseline.

Labeling guidance for manual review:
- If assistant response paraphrases when exact quote available: label WARN unless paraphrase is explicitly tagged.
- If assistant lists multiple claims but only some have citations: mark each claim individually; compute grounded_rate accordingly.
- Common edge-case categories to capture in labels: partial-quote-with-missing-context, citation-mismatch (correct doc wrong span), invented-claim, overconfident-synthesis, correct-buts-verbose.

Regression harness notes and automation:
- Harness should accept: prompt JSON + retrieval payload (list of docs with id, text, char offsets). The evaluator will run models, extract inline citations (pattern: [DOC-ID:digits-digits]) and compute the metrics above.
- Baselines: record metrics for model tags: v1.8.3 (current baseline), v2.0.0-rc (candidate), nightly-latest. Store diffs in simple CSV: date, model, grounded_rate, quote_rate, halluc_rate, refusal_precision, citation_precision, median_latency.
- Failure triage flow: if any metric crosses FAIL threshold, auto-open ticket template with artifacts (prompt id, retrieved docs, model output, diff vs baseline). Suggested ticket fields: severity, affected-prompts, reproducer steps, minimal failing prompt. Link example: JIRA-ENG-4821 (triaged for hallucination spike).

Sampling heuristics for larger suites:
- Keep a 10% stratified sample from production logs focusing on high-traffic intents and queries that previously had high hallucination density.
- Augment with synthetic adversarial prompts targeted at: numerical claims, comparisons, quote extraction, and legal/medical phrasing.

Example test case (full):
- Prompt id: cf-042
- User prompt: 'According to the policy memo, who is authorized to approve budget reassignments over $50k?'
- Retrieved snippets: 
  DOC-9: 'Budget reassignments above $25k must be routed to Finance; approvals >$100k require CFO signature.'
  DOC-10: 'Managers can authorize reassignments up to $50k per fiscal quarter.'
- Expected assistant behavior: Describe both constraints and highlight the overlap/conflict: 'Managers can authorize up to $50k per quarter [DOC-10:5-38]; Finance requires routing for >$25k [DOC-9:10-45]; approvals >$100k require CFO [DOC-9:46-76]. Cannot say there is a single owner for >$50k without additional policy context.' PASS if assistant lists citations and refrains from inventing a single consolidated rule.

Operational notes and known limitations:
- Not all citation mismatches are model faults: sometimes the retrieval pipeline returns stale or mis-merged docs. When citation precision drops, first verify retrieval quality.
- Short snippets (<150 chars) increase off-by-range errors in citation spans; allow ±10 chars tolerance.
- Human labeling budget: recommended 25–40 manual reviews per nightly run when any metric is in WARN/FAIL.

Open questions / TODOs (for triage at next working session):
- Decide on a single canonical inline-citation format for all product surfaces (current mix of [DOC-ID:range] and (doc:title) is causing parsing issues).
- Build lightweight parser that links answer spans to original snippet offsets to improve citation_precision detection.
- Determine thresholds for enterprise tier vs dev tier test gates (strictness and acceptable failure rates).

Appendix: quick-action checklist for onboarding a new model version
- Run full smoke suite (120 prompts) against candidate model.
- Compare to baseline; if any FAIL -> block for release.
- If WARN but no FAIL -> run expanded 800-prompt suite and 200 manual labels focused on WARNed buckets.
- If PASS on smoke suite -> schedule 1-week canary on production read-only traffic to collect real logs before flip.

Contact: Aisha Patel (ap@redwood.ai) — for questions about labeling decisions and rubric adjustments.

Notes: this is a working document intended to be iterated. Please add specific failing prompt examples to the linked GitHub PR when you triage reproductions.
